title: Design a search engine
prompt: Build the query-serving path for a web search engine. Traffic is brutally read-skewed: a small set of popular queries ("weather", "news") repeat millions of times, while a continuous crawl pipeline keeps mutating the index in the background. Draw how a query flows from the user, through an entry load balancer and query service, into a cache for hot result sets and a durable index as the source of truth — and show how newly crawled documents are ingested asynchronously through a queue so indexing never blocks the live query path. The dominant forcing constraint is read-skew on popular queries plus async index freshness.

criteria.label: Query originates from a user/client
criteria.metWhy: Good — the search flow starts from a real user typing a query.
criteria.why: Add a User/Client component as the entry point that issues the search query.

criteria.label: Traffic enters through a load balancer
criteria.metWhy: A load balancer or API gateway spreads query traffic across the service tier.
criteria.why: Millions of repeated queries hit one endpoint — add a Load Balancer or API Gateway in front of the query service to distribute load.

criteria.label: A query service handles search requests
criteria.metWhy: A dedicated query/compute tier parses the query and assembles results.
criteria.why: Add a Server or API/Service tier that receives the query, checks the cache, and queries the index.

criteria.label: Hot query results served from a cache
criteria.metWhy: A cache absorbs the read-skew — popular queries are answered without touching the index.
criteria.why: Read-skew dominates: a few queries repeat millions of times. Add a Cache for popular query result sets so the index isn't hit on every repeat.

criteria.label: Index/documents stored in a durable datastore
criteria.metWhy: A durable index is the source of truth for ranking and lookups.
criteria.why: Add a Database/index as the durable source of truth that the query service searches on a cache miss.

criteria.label: Service reads through the cache
criteria.metWhy: The read path checks the cache first — hot queries skip the index entirely.
criteria.why: Connect the query Service to the Cache so popular result sets are served before falling back to the index.

criteria.label: Service queries the index on a cache miss
criteria.metWhy: Cache misses fall back to the durable index for the actual lookup.
criteria.why: Connect the query Service to the Database/index so cold queries are resolved against the source of truth.

criteria.label: Crawled documents ingested asynchronously via a queue
criteria.metWhy: A queue decouples the crawl/indexing pipeline from live query serving.
criteria.why: The crawler keeps mutating the index — add a Queue so document ingestion happens asynchronously and never blocks the live query path.

criteria.label: System health is monitored
criteria.metWhy: Monitoring tracks query latency, cache hit rate, and indexing lag.
criteria.why: Add a Monitoring component to watch p99 query latency, cache hit ratio, and index freshness/lag.
